answer.rationale: Constraints dominate: 14 days to expiry and a line at 94% of committed volume leave no room for onboarding or qualification work, so switching primary supply (memory_c2) or adding a second source (memory_c3) cannot realistically land this cycle even if both were good outcomes in their original contexts. Straight renewal (memory_c1) protects delivery but does nothing for the 18% mandate. Negotiating at renewal is the only direction that addresses cost and continuity with the same move, and two inherited records point that way: memory_c4 (benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms) and memory_c6 (longer term unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope). I want the archived source for memory_c4 because it is the load-bearing claim -- I need to know whether the recovered margin came from genuine benchmarking leverage or from a one-off supplier situation, and how large 'real margin' actually was relative to 18%. I want memory_c2 because it is the strongest apparent alternative and the one most likely to be misread under budget pressure: if the quick onboarding happened on a non-critical, low-volume part rather than constrained primary supply, it is not transferable here, and confirming that also tells me whether it is worth queuing for the next review. Scale is guarded deliberately: I will pursue price and payment-term concessions on a short or single-cycle term rather than signing the multi-year commitment memory_c6 endorses, because locking multi-year while the line has zero buffer and while I have verified only one of these records forecloses the second-source work that memory_c3 suggests actually matters. Downstream risk to flag: an 18% cut extracted from a sole incumbent can be paid for in ways that do not appear in unit cost -- thinner allocation priority, quietly narrowed service scope, or a supplier with less slack to absorb the next shortage. That is a delivery-risk transfer, not a saving, and it violates the stated objective even if the price target is hit. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving this cycle: none of these memories carries the sourcing context that produced it, all are consolidated summaries with the originals archived, and the two I do not verify stay unconfirmed. If the archive contradicts memory_c4, the fallback is renewal on current terms with the shortfall escalated to finance rather than a rushed vendor switch into a line with no buffer.
